title: Orchestrated batch curator: workload fingerprinting, heuristic rule-set, and continuous safe-apply
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build an ‘Orchestrated Batch Curator’ that continuously profiles live workloads, derives compact workload fingerprints, synthesizes a prioritized heuristic rule-set for batching and KV-caching, and safely applies configuration adjustments through a staged rollout with automatic rollback triggers.

Why: We've observed 9–14% token-cost variance across similar services due to suboptimal batch sizes and stale cache policies. Manual tuning is slow and risky; this ticket scopes a system that automates recommendations and applies conservative changes with safety guards.

Scope / deliverables:
- Lightweight profiler agent that samples request streams and emits per-route fingerprints (request length distribution, inter-arrival distribution, KV-hit affinity, latency tail signals). Output format is a compact hash + histogram summary.
- Rule-set synthesizer that maps fingerprints -> candidate config deltas (batch_size caps, max_batch_latency_ms, kv_cache_ttl, prefix_cache_enabled). Use heuristics prioritized by expected cost delta and latency risk score.
- Continuous controller that schedules shadow experiments and can perform staged 'safe-apply' to a small % of traffic, measure quality/latency/cost signals, and either promote, widen, or rollback changes.
- Telemetry and guardrails: automated thresholds for rollback (p99 latency increase > 8% absolute or error-rate delta > 0.5%), and canary phases (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with min-observation windows.
- Audit and visibility: Console dashboard for per-route candidate suggestions, estimated cost delta, and rollout history with links to experiment traces.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Profiler produces <=1KB fingerprint per 1k requests and matches ground-truth when replayed in the lab (95% similarity on classification).
2) Synthesizer outputs conservative config deltas with predicted cost savings and a risk score.
3) Safe-apply mechanism can run a 1% canary and auto-rollback within 10 minutes on threshold breach.
4) End-to-end test: select 5 routes in staging; demonstrate net token-cost reduction >= 6% without p99 latency regression beyond thresholds.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We favor compact fingerprints over heavyweight ML models initially to ship quickly and keep explainability for SREs. If the heuristics plateau, we will iterate to a learned policy (future ticket).
- Cache TTL suggestions will avoid recommending prefix cache for routes with high output variance to reduce quality risk.
- Safety-first rollout: default promotion cadence is exponential; teams can opt for manual-promote if a route is high-risk.

Metrics to track:
- Cost-saved (tokens * price delta) per route
- p50/p95/p99 latency deltas pre/post apply
- Error rate and request quality checks (synthetic evaluation set where applicable)
- Number of auto-rollbacks and root causes

- Initial profiler prototype (notebooks + replay harness): drive:/redwood/infra/batch-curator/profiler-proto.ipynb
- Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/batch-curator-staging
- Related tickets: ENG-271144 (workload-curator safe apply), ENG-7421 (autotune-batching-profiles), ENG-24109 (dynamic-batch-configurator)

Open questions:
- How to represent cross-route KV affinity when a route fan-out touches multiple models? (proposal: attribute delta to originating route; follow-up to model affinity mapping.)
- Should the profiler sample for every request or run a reservoir sampling window per minute? Current plan: reservoir sampling with 10k window per route.
- How to surface quality regressions for open-ended generation routes? Current mitigation: require synthetic prompts and basic semantic similarity threshold before promotion.

Next steps:
- Finish profiler prototype and land initial telemetry ingestion (Liam)
- Implement synthesizer rule mappings and a simple scoring function (Aisha + backend)
- Build safe-apply controller skeleton and integrate with rollout engine (Reliability eng)
- Prepare staging experiment for 5 low-risk routes by 2026-03-20
